title: Config-file apiProxy.auth.provider rejects openai although the runtime supports OpenAI native WIF
symptoms: awf config validation reports that config.apiProxy.auth.provider must be one of azure, aws, gcp, anthropic
OpenAI native WIF works when AWF_AUTH_PROVIDER=openai is set in the environment but fails when the same value is set through the AWF config file
conditions: apiProxy.auth.type is github-oidc in the AWF config file
The failure is schema validation of the config file; the environment-variable path is not affected by this schema enum
rootCause: The published config schema (src/awf-config-schema.json, mirrored at docs/awf-config.schema.json) enumerates apiProxy.auth.provider as azure, aws, gcp, and anthropic only. validateAwfFileConfig() runs validateWithSchema() before any mapping, so a config file selecting openai is rejected even though the sidecar's cloud-oidc-init provider and the openai-credential-env agent routing accept AWF_AUTH_PROVIDER=openai.

probe.expect: Prints ["azure","aws","gcp","anthropic"] on a checkout that lacks openai in the schema enum. This reads only the bundled schema and never prints environment values, tokens, or Authorization headers.

action: Use the environment-variable form (AWF_AUTH_TYPE=github-oidc, AWF_AUTH_PROVIDER=openai, with AWF_AUTH_OPENAI_IDENTITY_PROVIDER_ID and AWF_AUTH_OPENAI_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_ID) until the schema enum is extended. The fix belongs in src/awf-config-schema.json and docs/awf-config.schema.json together, with schema tests; it is not verified here. Do not put the OpenAI IDs into the agent environment or work around the schema by editing generated artifacts.

references.title: Add OpenAI workload identity federation to the API proxy
